query: Vince Phillips held a junior welterweight title by an organization recognized by what larger Hall of Fame?

pipeline_result.response: Vince Phillips held a junior welterweight title by the IBF and WBO organizations, which are recognized by the United States Boxing Hall of Fame.
retrieved_context: Vince Phillips: Vincent Edwards "Vince" Phillips (born July 23, 1963) is an American former professional boxer who competed from 1989 to 2007.  He held the IBF junior welterweight title from 1997 to 1999, notably scoring an upset victory against then-undefeated Kostya Tszyu to become champion.

Ultimate Fighting Championship: The Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is an American mixed martial arts organization based in Las Vegas, Nevada, that is owned and operated by parent company WME–IMG.  It is the largest MMA promotion in the world and features the top-ranked fighters of the sport.  Based in the United States, the UFC produces events worldwide that showcase eleven weight divisions and abide by the Unified Rules of Mixed Martial Arts.  As of 2017, the UFC has held over 400 events.  Dana White serves as the president of the UFC.  He has held that position since 2001; while under the leadership of Dana White the UFC has grown into a globally popular multibillion-dollar enterprise.

Zab Judah: Zabdiel Judah (born October 27, 1977) is an American professional boxer.  He is a four-time former world champion in two weight classes, having held the IBF and WBO junior welterweight titles between 2000 and 2004; the IBF junior welterweight title again in 2011; and the undisputed welterweight title in 2005, which included a reign as the lineal champion from 2005 to 2006.
